title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving multisectoral GBV response, prevention and risk mitigation to crisis affected populations in the North West, South West & Far North regions of Cameroon

description.narrative: UNFPA will use the CERF funds to implement lifesaving Gender Based Violence (GBV) protection and Sexual and Reproductive Health services in Far North, North-West and South-West regions of Cameroon reaching 84,180 women, girls, men and boys. The proposed intervention is based on evidence, lessons learnt and gaps identified in the humanitarian response in those regions of Cameroon. UNFPA intends to scale up life-saving SRH and GBV response to expand coverage and to meet the increasing needs of the affected population, including those in hard-to-reach areas. UNFPA will use the survivors centered approach across different interventions, to ensure services are inclusive and provided in a way to reach all vulnerable populations including persons living with disabilities and other minorities.The key objective of this project is to save lives and alleviate suffering in crisis-affected regions of Cameroon through the provision of essential SRH and GBV services to the most vulnerable people in hard-to-reach areas.UNFPA is expecting to realize the following outputs:1.Increased access to safe and confidential GBV survivor-centred comprehensive case management services 2. Increased GBV prevention and risk mitigation through risk analysis, awareness raising, dignity distribution to women and girls3. SRH services provision including MISP for is reinforced and increased in supported health facilities4. Reinforced information and community mobilization on SRHSRH service package will include BeMonc and CeMonc services, deployment of midwives, clinical management of rape, outreach and community mobilization. To maximize impact UNFPA will conduct capacity building on SRH components to increase the quality of services. In addition, will deploy humanitarian midwives to ensure supported health facilities have recommended workforce to support clients. UNFPA will also ensure the acquisition and last mile distribution of essential emergency IARH kits. To further increase the reach, UNFPA will deploy integrated mobile clinics to reach the hard to reach and most vulnerable people and will use cash to improve referral services. UNFPA will support the establishment of maternity waiting home to improve women access to quality maternal services. UNFPA will continue to distribute baby boxes to increase the SRH services demand.For Gender Based violence, UNFPA will continue to support the establishment of WGSS which has proved to be corner stone GBV reporting. UNFPA will support the provision of quality and comprehensive GBV case management including MHPSS, and referrals to health facilities for Clinical management of rape. Services will be provided within the Women and Girls Safe Spaces, mobile clinics and health facilities to meet the needs of the survivors and in line with quality standards. UNFPA will leverage internal expertise to establish strong referral pathways so that survivors can access both MHPSS and medical services provided by UNFPA and other services based on the survivors needs, wishes and choice. As part as GBV prevention and risk mitigation, UNFPA will distribute dignity kits to women and girls most in need and will continue to use safety audits findings to inform risks mitigation plan at different levels. UNFPA will continue to engage in partnership with various national actors to ensure successful implementation activities. UNFPA intends to work with the following IPs: ALVF, ALDEPA, WA CAMEROON, CBCHS and will continue to support the key government counterpart namely the regional delegation of health as well as Ministry of women empowerment and the family. UNFPA is identifying another IP to support the project implementation in South West region.
